text:
alina: heads-up: i prototyped a 'slab fusion' variant to pack many tiny prefixes into a shared slab while preserving per-tenant eviction semantics. goal: cut fragmentation for lots of 1-8KB prefixes without a full refactor. high-level notes below, want quick sanity check.

alina: approach: adjacent small slabs can be merged into a fusion slab. items keep tenant tags and a small per-tenant refcount in slab metadata. eviction operates at tenant-level by acquiring the fusion slab lease and decrementing the tenant refcounts; physical reclaim is a later compaction step.

dexter: main worry is cross-node correctness during reclaim. if the lease owner dies mid-reclaim we could reclaim another tenant's live keys, or reads could rehydrate items that were just marked for reclaim. how does the protocol avoid that?

alina: we make reclaim two-phase: (1) jot a reclaim mark in slab metadata: (tenant_id, reclaim_uuid, slab_epoch). that mark is idempotent and replicated. (2) background compaction reads marks, verifies no active leases (using lease_epoch) for that tenant, then frees entries. if a node dies mid-step other nodes see the mark and either complete or skip based on epoch checks.

maria: what's the minimal atomic primitive? do we need a global epoch generator?

chen: propose slab_epoch monotonic counter per-slab. any mark includes slab_epoch and reclaim_uuid. readers compare slab_epoch with their lease_epoch: if slab_epoch < lease_epoch they must treat entries as potentially stale and avoid serving them. also we should ensure reclaim_uuid is unique (uuid v4).

dexter: readers refusing to serve when slab_epoch < lease_epoch seems strict. could that cause availability blips?

alina: it's conservative: only when a reader's lease is newer than the slab epoch. the common case is no bump, so no issue. bumps happen during reclaim/compaction windows. we can instrument and relax later if too noisy.

tomas: perf impact? fusion adds a small indirection (offset table and tenant-tag lookup). microbench on a devbox: single-key GET p95 ~5-7% slower, memory usage for tiny-prefix workloads improved ~15-20%. for mid/large prefixes there's no change.
maria: need per-tenant opt-out and automated policy so premium/high-qps tenants avoid fusion.
alina: yes: tenant flag + autopolicy: fusion for tenants with median prefix <= 6KB AND qps < threshold. operator CLI to toggle on tenant and region scope.

chen: rollback story? we must support fast rollback if canary shows correctness issues.
alina: feature flag gating + an explicit split-compaction command. rollback flips the flag and triggers compaction that rewrites fused slab into per-tenant slabs. compaction is idempotent and writes redirect mappings for a TTL so existing cursors can be resolved.
maria: cursors & long-lived reads: how do we avoid breaking them?

alina: cursors carry (slab_id, offset, lease_epoch). during split compaction we keep a redirect map from old (slab_id, offset) -> new (slab_id, offset) for N minutes. if a cursor hits a relocated offset inside that TTL, we rewrite transparently. outside TTL we return 409 to force client retry.
dexter: tests? add chaos tests that force kill reclaim-holder and concurrent read+compaction races. also add integration sim for epoch bumping path.
alina: agreed. i'll add: epoch bump in simulated reclaim, redirect map behavior, and a chaos scenario to CI. ops-bot: can you run a targeted chaos after next canary?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary build 1771.3 deployed to canary eu-west-1 at 1771005588. CI: unit 124 passed, integration smoke basic-prefetch 11/12 passed (one flaky prefetch test still failing). scheduling chaos run on request.

maria: metrics and alerts to detect silent data-loss or stale reads?
alina: plan metrics: slab_fusion_marked_reclaims, slab_fusion_completed_reclaims, slab_fusion_compaction_errors, slab_epoch_mismatch_count, slab_fusion_redirect_hits, slab_fusion_redirect_misses. sample high-cardinality logs for reclaim_uuid failures at 1/1000.

chen: add an invariant check in debug builds: after reclaim complete, a scan verifies no live keys for tenant in slab (sampling mode in prod only after opt-in).
dexter: operator playbook: (1) flip feature flag to canary range; (2) watch metrics for N minutes; (3) on reclaim_conflict spike -> flip flag off, trigger split-compaction, wait for redirects TTL, force nodes to reload slab metadata. document exact thresholds.
alina: will write RFC follow-up with diagrams, the state machine (mark -> compact -> free), the invariants (lease_epoch monotonicity, reclaim_uuid uniqueness, redirect TTL), the test plan, and the operator steps. target: post EOD tomorrow.

tomas: i can help review playbook, esp rollback steps.
alina: thanks! last note: we'll only enable fusion for low-cost tenants initially and expand if stable. will update thread when RFC follow-up is up.
